_note: SYNTHETIC underwriting guidelines written for this demo. They are not any insurer's real guidelines, and contain no confidential material.

chunks.title: Flood exposure
chunks.text: Locations on a mapped river or coastal flood plain, or with a flood event in the last 10 years, must be referred to a senior underwriter. A commercial location on a flood plain with a total insured value above EUR 2 million and no installed flood defences is CRITICAL. A location outside any mapped flood zone with no flood history carries no flood loading and is LOW for this factor.

chunks.title: Construction type and age
chunks.text: Standard masonry or brick construction built after 2000 is rated at standard terms (LOW). Buildings constructed before 1980, and timber-frame, thatch or flat-roof construction, are HIGH unless a satisfactory electrical and roof survey from the last 5 years is provided.

chunks.title: Prior claims history
chunks.text: Three or more claims in the last 5 years, or any single claim above EUR 100,000, makes the risk MEDIUM at minimum, and HIGH where the cause of loss has not been remedied. No prior claims is LOW for this factor.

chunks.title: Subsidence and ground conditions
chunks.text: Known subsidence, mining activity, landfill or unstable ground at or near the location is HIGH. An explicit statement that there is no history of subsidence is LOW for this factor. Absence of information is not evidence of subsidence.

chunks.title: Fire protection
chunks.text: Sprinklers or a monitored fire alarm reduce the fire rating by one tier. Commercial premises above EUR 1 million total insured value with no fire protection raise the rating by one tier.

chunks.title: Sum insured against financial standing
chunks.text: A sum insured above ten times annual turnover or net assets, without explanation, is HIGH. A newly formed entity with no trading history requesting more than EUR 1 million is HIGH, and CRITICAL where the sum insured exceeds EUR 5 million.

chunks.title: Financial documentation
chunks.text: Commercial applicants with a total insured value above EUR 2 million must provide three years of audited accounts. Missing audited accounts make the financial risk MEDIUM at minimum.

chunks.title: Standard residential applicants
chunks.text: Individual residential applicants with a sum insured under EUR 1 million and no adverse credit indicators are LOW financial risk.

chunks.title: Single-risk concentration
chunks.text: Any single-risk exposure above EUR 5 million requires senior sign-off regardless of other factors, and must be referred.

chunks.title: Sanctions
chunks.text: Any applicant, beneficial owner or employer connected to a jurisdiction, entity or individual on the EU, UN or OFAC consolidated sanctions lists is CRITICAL. The risk must not be bound and must be referred to compliance.

chunks.title: Regulatory investigations and AML
chunks.text: An open regulatory investigation, enforcement action or anti-money-laundering flag against the applicant, beneficial owner or their employer is HIGH at minimum, and CRITICAL where it concerns financial crime.

chunks.title: Politically exposed persons
chunks.text: A politically exposed person requires enhanced due diligence and is MEDIUM at minimum.

chunks.title: No adverse indicators
chunks.text: Where no sanctions, investigation, AML or PEP indicators are present, the regulatory risk is LOW. Missing information about these matters is not itself an adverse indicator.

chunks.title: Reading negation and absence
chunks.text: A statement that a hazard is absent, such as not in a flood zone, no claims, or no history of subsidence, means the hazard is absent and must not be scored as if it were present.

chunks.title: Consolidation rule
chunks.text: The consolidated risk level is the worst of the property, financial and regulatory assessments, never an average. A single HIGH or CRITICAL dimension makes the whole submission a referral.
